components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: A compact filter that can be scanned and toggled quickly.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; min-height: 40px; padding: 10px 14px; border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-radius: 9999px; background: #F3F3F3; color: #6B6B6B; font: 600 12px/1.2 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out, color 150ms ease-out, border-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-chip-active { border-color: #0B0B0B; background: #0B0B0B; color: #FFFFFF; } .ds-chip:hover { border-color: #0B0B0B; color: #0B0B0B; } .ds-chip-active:hover { background: #242424; color: #FFFFFF; } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(47, 111, 237, .38); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Map Control

components.css: .ds-map-control { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 48px; height: 48px; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: #FFFFFF; color: #0B0B0B; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, .12); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out, box-shadow 200ms ease, transform 150ms ease-out; } .ds-map-control svg { width: 21px; height: 21px; fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.8; stroke-linecap: round; } .ds-map-control:hover { box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(0, 0, 0, .18); } .ds-map-control:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(47, 111, 237, .38); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-map-control:active { transform: scale(.96); }

narrative.overview:
Court Finder should feel like a dependable field instrument for someone standing somewhere unfamiliar. The interface is calm at rest, immediate when action is needed, and specific about what the system actually knows. It borrows the directness of mature mobility apps—destination-first search, a map that stays available beneath the task, and focused sheets that keep the next decision close—without copying another company's branding, assets, typography, or iconography.

The visual world is mostly neutral: carbon, paper, fog, and utility gray give the map and satellite imagery room to speak. Bold accents are reserved for actions, facility types, route-like movement, and explicit state. A possible facility is treated like a field note: useful evidence to inspect, never a promise of access, availability, safety, or accuracy.

The intended target is a mobile-first operating experience. Controls are direct and tactile, with generous touch targets, short labels, strong contrast, and bottom sheets that bring detail into reach. Depth is hybrid: the map and content stay visually quiet, while search, controls, result sheets, and primary actions lift clearly above the surface.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral carbon-and-paper foundation with deliberate signal color.
Direct, tactile controls sized for thumbs before pointers.
Confidence and verification treated as evidence, not decoration.
Light and dark themes share the same hierarchy and semantic roles.

rules.name: The Neutral Canvas Rule
rules.body: Keep the majority of every screen carbon, paper, fog, or utility gray. Color earns its place by signaling an action, category, or state.

rules.name: The Evidence Color Rule
rules.body: A bright marker identifies a facility type or interaction state; it never implies that a detection is accurate, public, open, safe, or available.

rules.name: The One-Decision Rule
rules.body: A heading, sheet, or action group should make its next decision obvious before secondary explanation appears.

rules.name: The Lift-on-Task Rule
rules.body: Elevation belongs to something the person can act on. Do not add shadow merely to make a passive container look finished.

dos: Do keep most of the screen neutral and let one signal color define the next action.
Do make primary controls at least 48px tall and easy to operate with a thumb.
Do keep the map visible or one gesture away while people search, filter, and inspect.
Do use facility colors consistently across markers, chips, legends, and detail views.
Do show satellite context, confidence, and verification status as separate pieces of evidence.
Do use direct language such as “possible facility,” “model confidence,” and “verify access.”
donts: Don't introduce borrowed brand assets, proprietary fonts, or branded component patterns; the system should feel native to Court Finder.
Don't flood a screen with orange, blue, or facility colors; saturation is a signal with a job.
Don't make every control a pill or every surface a floating card.
Don't use gradients, glass blur, or decorative shadows when a neutral surface and clear hierarchy are enough.
Don't describe a detection or confidence score as proof of accuracy, public access, availability, safety, or permission to enter.
Don't let a marketing treatment obscure the operating task: search, inspect, verify, decide.
